verdicts.quote: After save, the nurse sees a confirmation that the note was successfully written to both the EHR and the spreadsheet, with a unique note ID and a 10-second sync status indicator that turns green when complete.

When a charge nurse flags a discrepancy, they cannot edit the original note—only annotate it with a status label like "Review Pending" or "Discrepancy Identified"—and assign it to the originating nurse via a workflow in the app.

The unit manager reviews the EHR entry and approves an override to show the note as "Validated" in the spreadsheet, with an audit trail noting "override applied due to 15-minute EHR-to-spreadsheet delay during network failure."
At the start of a shift, a nurse logs in via Azure AD SSO, which redirects them to the ward note dashboard showing their assigned patients and any pending notes from the previous shift.
Charge nurses will use the tool to review all ward notes for their unit daily, filtering by patient, nurse, or time range to verify completeness and flag discrepancies.
